analysis:
Reviewed unit 0 and the replayed patches/metadata for .github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml, changelog.d/darkbloom-watchdog-listing-size.md and docs/developer/build.md. Workflow HEAD:112-138,194-198 replaces jq command-line JSON arguments with file/stdin aggregation, retaining the visible pagination limits. This addresses argument-size failures; no new shell evaluation or credential exposure is evident in the change.
Workflow HEAD:229-242 broadens rescue eligibility: recent completions no longer block cancellation, and an old queued job is timed from its own creation even when other jobs remain running. Changelog HEAD:4-5 and build documentation HEAD:442-448 accurately describe this behavior and its inability to distinguish intentional resource-limit waits. No supplied evidence establishes an exploitable security regression from that ambiguity.
The changes do not modify provider authorization, attestation, encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing or privileged local controls. This GitHub workflow is distinct from the provider rollback watchdog covered by T-043. Release integrity assets A-011/A-017 remain relevant indirectly: integration should verify that cancelling partially completed build/publication work and rerunning it preserves publication consistency and selects the intended fallback runners. Those implementations are not supplied, so unsafe fallback or duplicate publication cannot be asserted. Replay omits two previously reviewed source units, preventing independent verification of surrounding rescue safeguards described in the local analysis; this coverage limit and the changed cancellation/retry contract require further review, not a vulnerability finding.
